text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The cabinet of Guntars Krasts was approved by parliament by 73 votes for and 13 against.

- Latvian and Russian delegations approved a draft border agreement after two days of talks. But the document has no reference to a 1920 peace treaty between Latvia and Russia, which may cause problems when it comes to ratifying the deal.
- Prices in July were up by 0.5 percent.

- Defence Minister Talavs Jundzis issued an order urging Latvian military officers to choose between serving in the Latvian army or receiving a pension from Russia, which is paid to some former Soviet army officers.
- A conference "Women and Men in Dialogue" with nearly 1,500 participants from 11 countries opened in the northern town of Valmiera.
- Major fuel trading companies in Latvia have announced a rise in fuel retail prices.

- Two Latvian banks - Rietumu Banka and Parex Bank gained a partial victory over Russia's tax authority as arbitration courts in St Petersburg and Moscow banned on Thursday Russia's tax authority from charging off the two banks correspondent accounts.
- The exchange rate of the dollar rose to 0.60 per to one lat. Experts say one buyer bought $20 and $30 million in recent days.
- Ventspils Nafta reported a 170,000 tonne increase in oil shipments in July versus the previous month.
- Norway's Hakon opened a second Rimi food supermarket.
- The privatization agency has started publishing a new monthly periodical of privatisation news.
